subject: MAP: MedFlow evaluation cadence & Dedicated capacity sizing
messages:
From: Helen Cho <helen.cho@medflow.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP & evaluation cadence for Dedicated capacity — MedFlow

Rishi / Laura,

Thanks for taking time last week. We're ready to formalize a mutual action plan so we can move an evaluation to a committed Reserved/Dedicated capacity purchase. Attached is our internal evaluation checklist to help map acceptance criteria. High-level asks from our side:

- Target evaluation window: two full weeks of production-like load.
- Preferred start: Oct 11
- Need clarity on Dedicated lead times and how quickly Redwood can allocate a GPU tranche after we commit.
- Guidance on recommended GPU pool sizing for our workload (we're running batching for clinical note summarization, avg seq len ~1,200 tokens, peak QPS ~14 req/s).

Can you outline a proposed MAP (milestones, owners, dates) and call out any gating items (SOC2, data residency, contract wording) that will affect timing? Also please flag any assumptions you need from us.

I've attached our Eval checklist. I'll loop procurement (procurement@medflow.ai) once we have a draft MAP.

Thanks,
Helen Cho
VP Product
MedFlow

Attachments: MedFlow-Eval-Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 45KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Cho <helen.cho@medflow.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & evaluation cadence for Dedicated capacity — MedFlow

Helen — thanks, this is clear and helpful. Drafting a concise MAP for your team and internal stakeholders; key points below (high level). I attached a one-page MAP draft and a SOC2 summary.

Proposed MAP (summary):
- Kickoff: Tech sync + environment access — week of Oct 11 (owner: MedFlow + Redwood SE)
- Eval window: Oct 12–25 (2 weeks) — acceptance tests defined by MedFlow checklist items A1..A6
- Performance tuning/observability: continuous during eval (Redwood Console dashboard + token-level traces)
- Acceptance decision: Oct 26 meeting (pass/fail + list of defects)
- Commitment target: Nov 15 — sign SOW & initial Dedicated tranche allocation

Lead time notes (assumptions called out):
- Hosted/Dedicated tranche allocation: after signed commit we can provision a reserved tranche from our pool in ~2–3 business days if capacity available; if new GPUs are required (customer-dedicated on a new physical pool), procurement & provisioning lead time is ~10–12 weeks (hardware lead times + setup).
- Private on-prem deployment (customer-managed infra): typical integration and on-prem bundle delivery 8–10 weeks depending on network / KMS setup.

Sizing guidance (initial recommendation based on your provided load):
- Eval (staging): 2 x A100-80GB equiv (single-tranche ephemeral) — supports short bursts with batching and prefix cache.
- Production initial tranche: 4 x A100-80GB equiv for steady-state low-latency throughput, with autoscale to burst pool.
- Canary / rollouts: keep a 10–15% buffer in burst headroom; use prefix KV cache to reduce repeated prompt cost.

Next steps I propose:
1) 60-minute tech walkthrough (Redwood infra + test harness) — Tue Oct 6 @ 10:00am PT?
2) You share the usage estimates CSV and any compliance reqs we should pre-populate in the MAP
3) I'll update the MAP PDF with GPU sizing assumptions and send a version for procurement/legal.

Attached: MAP-draft-MedFlow.pdf, SOC2-Redwood-summary.pdf

Adding a couple of operational clarifications so procurement/legal have clear expectations:

- Sizing assumptions we used for the draft: average sequence length 1,200 tokens, avg latency budget 200–500ms, batching window 40ms. If your actual latency budget is stricter we should increase the production tranche size.
- For the production tranche recommendation (4x A100-80GB equiv), that assumes 70% utilization and intelligent batching. If you expect sustained peaks >30 QPS we should plan a second tranche for immediate failover.
- Acceptance gating: please confirm which checklist items are must-pass for go/no-go (e.g., data egress, encryption at rest, audit logging). Those items will determine whether we can sign a standard SOW or need addenda.

Operational playbook note: we'll provision a staging slice that mirrors the prod config (same quantization profile and KV cache settings) to ensure fidelity. Marissa: please prep a checklist for the on-call handover during the eval (alerts, escalation matrix). Ben: can you scope the SOW draft once the MAP is finalized?
